draft.title: Structure and features of spoken texts
card: A speech is built in stages so a listener can follow it by ear. It usually opens to win attention, builds its case in the middle, and ends with a clear final message.
Anecdote
a short personal story. It makes an idea feel real and helps the audience connect with the speaker.
Pause
a deliberate silence. It gives listeners time to think and can add weight to the words just before or after it.
Repetition
saying a word or phrase more than once. It makes a main point easy to remember and can build energy.
draft.remember: A speech is shaped for listeners, and each feature is chosen for its effect on them.

a.q: A speaker says that we must listen, we must learn, and we must change, starting each part with the same three words. What is the main effect of this repetition?
opts: It makes the main message stick in listeners' minds
It gives listeners time to think in silence
It tells a personal story about the speaker's life
It opens the speech to win the audience's attention
a.why: Starting each part with the same words drives one message home and makes it easy to remember. A pause is a silence, not repeated words, so it is not the best answer.
a.clue: Look at which words keep coming back.

b.q: Nina begins her school captain speech by describing how she once froze on stage and a friend helped her. Which feature is this, and what does it do?
opts: An anecdote, which helps the audience connect with her
Repetition, which makes her main point easy to remember
A pause, which gives listeners time to think
An anecdote, which gives listeners time to think in silence
b.why: Nina tells a short personal story, so it is an anecdote. Such stories help the audience feel close to the speaker. Giving listeners time to think is the effect of a pause, not of a story.
b.clue: Is she telling a short story from her own life?

a.best: It makes the main message stick in listeners' minds

b.best: An anecdote, which helps the audience connect with her
